beats.label: S1 · Funeral summons
beats.text: Estranged siblings reunite for their father Reginald Hargreeves' funeral; Number Five reappears from the future warning the world will end in eight days.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the family, the ticking clock, and Five as the plot engine — every S2 opening beat assumes the reader knows Five is the time-traveller with a doomsday deadline.

beats.label: S1 · Assassins and Vietnam
beats.text: Commission killers Hazel and Cha-Cha hunt Five and abduct Klaus, whose escape via briefcase strands him in Vietnam, where he falls for a soldier named Dave.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Dave is the emotional anchor Klaus chases in S2's Dallas timeline; without this the S2 paint-store scene is meaningless.

beats.label: S1 · Five's employer, Five's target
beats.text: Five's Commission past is revealed — he was the Handler's top assassin. From a prosthetic eye he identifies Harold Jenkins as the man who triggers the apocalypse.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Commission and the Handler become S2's central antagonist infrastructure; the audience needs to know Five walked out on them.

beats.label: S1 · Leonard wakes the violin
beats.text: Harold Jenkins, posing as violin student Leonard, manipulates Vanya off her medication; her long-suppressed reality-warping powers begin to surface.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Vanya's powers are the single fact that drives every subsequent season's apocalypse math — this is where they exit dormancy.

beats.label: S1 · The diary and the throat
beats.text: Vanya slashes Allison's throat with her power after Allison confesses Reginald had her rumored ordinary; later she finds Reginald's diary and kills Leonard in a rage.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Allison is mute at the start of S2 and why the sibling trust in Vanya is broken going into the finale — and into every rebuild after.

beats.label: S1 · The chamber and the break
beats.text: Luther locks Vanya in the mansion's isolation chamber to contain her. She breaks free, destroys the mansion, and kills Pogo and Grace on her way out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cage is the decision that tips her from unstable to catastrophic — the moment the family loses her rather than saves her.

beats.label: S1 · Moon breaks, siblings jump
beats.text: At the Icarus Theatre, Vanya's unleashed energy shatters the moon and ends the world; Five time-jumps the siblings into the past to try the ending again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the exact launchpad into S2 — the reader must arrive knowing why they land scattered in the past and why 'this time fix Vanya' is the plan.

cliffhanger.text: The moon has been shattered by Vanya's power and the world has ended. Five has yanked the siblings into the past mid-apocalypse to try again — but nobody knows where or when they landed, or whether they can control Vanya before she does it a second time.
questions: Where and when did each sibling land after the jump?
Can Vanya be reached before her powers detonate again?
With the Commission still hunting Five, is the past any safer than the future?

characters.name: Number Five
characters.line: 58-year-old man in a 13-year-old body, ex-Commission assassin, and the only reason anyone in the family knows the apocalypse is coming.

characters.name: Luther (Number One)
characters.line: Team leader whose body was ape-transformed by a serum after a botched mission; in love with Allison and the one who chose to cage Vanya.

characters.name: Diego (Number Two)
characters.line: Knife-throwing vigilante estranged from the family, still grieving Detective Patch and freshly cleared of her murder.

characters.name: Allison (Number Three)
characters.line: Reality-bending 'rumor' powers, now mute after Vanya slashed her throat; she used Reginald's request to convince Vanya she was ordinary as a child.

characters.name: Klaus (Number Four)
characters.line: Medium who talks to the dead; sober-ish and freshly traumatised by losing Dave in a Vietnam tour he took via briefcase.

characters.name: Vanya (Number Seven)
characters.line: Believed powerless her whole life; is actually the most powerful of them and just caused the apocalypse she was medicated to prevent.

characters.name: Ben (Number Six)
characters.line: The dead brother; a ghost tethered to Klaus and only visible to him.

characters.name: The Handler
characters.line: Commission executive who ran Five as her hitman; shot by Hazel at the bowling alley when her offer to Hazel turned out to be a lie.

characters.name: Hazel
characters.line: Ex-Commission killer who defected for the doughnut waitress Agnes; helped clear Diego and escaped into the past with her.

beats.label: S2 · Scattered across Dallas
beats.text: The time jump strands the siblings across Dallas between 1960 and 1963; Five arrives days before a Soviet nuclear doomsday he must stop.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The scattered-family, ticking-clock, wrong-decade premise is what every subsequent beat depends on and what S3's return has to undo.

beats.label: S2 · New lives in the wrong decade
beats.text: Siblings settle into new lives: Vanya nannies Sissy's son Harlan, Allison marries activist Ray, Klaus leads a cult, Luther guards Jack Ruby, Diego is committed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Harlan and Sissy in particular are load-bearing for later — Harlan is where Vanya's power residue ends up.

beats.label: S2 · The Handler and her daughter
beats.text: The Handler survived Hazel's bullet and returns to power; she plants her adoptive daughter Lila — secretly another of the '43' children — on Diego to shadow Five.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Lila, whose survival at S2's end sets up her role in every later season, and re-installs the Handler as the season's antagonist.

beats.label: S2 · Reginald unmasks
beats.text: Reginald is in Dallas convening the shadowy Majestic 12; after JFK still dies he peels off his human face, revealing himself as an alien, and kills them all.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reginald being alive in 1963 and being non-human are both facts that fundamentally reshape how the family reads him from here on.

beats.label: S2 · Vanya remembers, JFK doesn't die
beats.text: FBI torture cracks Vanya's memory and unleashes an explosion that stops JFK's assassination — starting World War III as the second apocalypse in ten days.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Second apocalypse, same cause. This is the beat that proves 'fix Vanya' was the wrong plan.

beats.label: S2 · Ben goes
beats.text: Ben possesses Klaus's body to reach Vanya from inside her mind and calm her, averting the apocalypse — and is then finally pulled to the afterlife.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The dead brother leaving is the emotional pivot of the season and the reason the S3 opening reveal of a living Ben lands so hard.

beats.label: S2 · Home is wrong
beats.text: Axel kills the Handler; Vanya reclaims her powers, leaving Harlan a residue. Herb sends them home to a 2019 where Reginald raised the Sparrow Academy — and Ben is alive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the entire launchpad into S3: altered timeline, a rival Academy, and a living Ben. Also plants the Harlan residue that becomes S3's paradox.

cliffhanger.text: The siblings finally make it back to 2019 — except it isn't theirs. Reginald raised a completely different team called the Sparrow Academy, Ben is alive and hostile, and the family they knew here has been erased.
questions: What did the siblings' return trigger in this altered timeline?
Who are these seven Sparrows, and why did Reginald prefer them?
If Ben is alive here, does he remember the brothers standing in front of him?

characters.name: Number Five
characters.line: Still 13-bodied, now the closest thing the Commission has to a defector; brought the siblings home into a timeline he didn't intend.

characters.name: Luther
characters.line: Ape-bodied bodyguard turned romantic; his S1 grudge against Vanya has thawed and he's the one who first sees this timeline is wrong.

characters.name: Diego
characters.line: Just left Lila, whom he loved and who turned out to be Commission.

characters.name: Allison
characters.line: Voice has healed; leaves behind a civil-rights husband Ray and returns to 2019 alone, capable of using her rumor powers again.

characters.name: Klaus
characters.line: No longer a ghost's chaperone — Ben has moved on. Left behind Dave, the cult he built, and Axel who joined it.

characters.name: Vanya
characters.line: Powers back, memory intact, and now aware she caused two apocalypses; walked away from Sissy and Harlan to keep them safe.

characters.name: Reginald Hargreeves
characters.line: Alive in 2019 in this timeline; revealed to be an alien and has raised a different set of children in the family's absence.

characters.name: Lila
characters.line: Handler's adoptive daughter and one of the 43 special children; mimics any power near her, and escaped Dallas alive after learning her mother had her parents killed.

characters.name: Harlan Cooper
characters.line: Sissy's son; Vanya's powers were transferred into him and then reclaimed, but she left him with a residue she couldn't fully take back.

characters.name: Ben
characters.line: As a ghost, finally departed for the afterlife after possessing Klaus to save Vanya — but is alive and hostile as a Sparrow in the 2019 they've just landed in.

beats.label: S3 · Wrong timeline, wrong siblings
beats.text: The Umbrella siblings crash into the Sparrow Academy timeline, lose the fight, and shelter at Hotel Obsidian; Sparrow leader Marcus is disintegrated by an emerging Kugelblitz.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes both this season's rival family and the physical apocalypse (the Kugelblitz) that is going to consume reality until the reset.

beats.label: S3 · Viktor, and no Claire
beats.text: Vanya comes out as transgender and takes the name Viktor. Allison learns her daughter Claire has been erased from this timeline and begins to spiral.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Viktor's identity carries forward, and Allison's spiral over Claire is the single motivation behind the season-ending betrayal.

beats.label: S3 · A paradox eating the world
beats.text: The Kugelblitz begins deleting people and matter; Five ties it to a grandfather paradox — the siblings' mothers all died before pregnancy in this timeline.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The stakes for the whole season are now concrete: their existence itself is the apocalypse this time.

beats.label: S3 · Harlan, and revenge
beats.text: Harlan resurfaces as Lester Pocket and confesses his outburst on Sissy's death killed the mothers and caused the paradox; Allison murders him for erasing Claire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The paradox's origin closes and Allison crosses a moral line — the crossing is what makes her S3 finale deal with Reginald plausible.

beats.label: S3 · Klaus is immortal
beats.text: Klaus dies and revives repeatedly, learning he simply cannot stay dead; he starts bonding with the medicated Sparrow-timeline Reginald.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Klaus's immortality is a hard fact the reader needs walking into S4 — his S4 predicament assumes it.

beats.label: S3 · A reset behind seven bells
beats.text: Reginald reveals Hotel Obsidian hides a portal to Hotel Oblivion and a universe reset button behind seven bells; he murders Luther to force the group to cross.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the season's plot mechanism and Reginald's true agenda — everything the finale does is a reaction to it.

beats.label: S3 · Reset, and a stranger's world
beats.text: Allison — secretly in her own deal with Reginald — axe-kills him and hits the reset. The universe reboots powerless, Sloane vanished, and a new Reginald ruling with a revived Abigail.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The launchpad into S4: no powers, Reginald in charge of the world, and Abigail alive. Every S4 opening beat depends on this state.

cliffhanger.text: Allison's secret deal with Reginald has rebooted the universe. The siblings are alive and scattered but stripped of their powers, Luther's body is human again, Sloane is missing, and a new Reginald is running the city with a resurrected wife nobody has met before. In a mid-credits shot, Ben rides a Seoul subway to a destination he hasn't explained.
questions: What are the new Reginald and Abigail actually building in the city they now control?
Where is Sloane, and can Luther find her without powers to search with?
Where is Ben going, and does he remember either family?

characters.name: Number Five
characters.line: Arm regrown by the reset; still 13-bodied and the one who first exposed Allison's private deal with Reginald.

characters.name: Luther
characters.line: Human body restored by the reset; married Sloane during the season and lost her when the universe rebooted.

characters.name: Diego
characters.line: With Lila again and about to be a father; his son Stan turned out to be a borrowed nephew Lila used to test him.

characters.name: Allison
characters.line: Reunited with Claire and Ray thanks to her secret deal with Reginald; by season's end Viktor knows about the deal.

characters.name: Klaus
characters.line: Discovered he is immortal — no matter how he dies he comes back — and finally reconciled a little with Reginald.

characters.name: Viktor
characters.line: Formerly Vanya; transitioned this season and now grieving Harlan, whom Allison killed for causing the paradox.

characters.name: Lila
characters.line: Back with Diego and pregnant with his child; can still mimic any power near her, though the reset has taken powers off the table for now.

characters.name: Ben
characters.line: Was the leader of the Sparrow Academy this timeline; alive after the reset and last seen riding a Seoul subway alone.

characters.name: Reginald Hargreeves
characters.line: The reset-timeline version, now openly ruling the city with his revived wife — no longer an eccentric benefactor, a sovereign.

characters.name: Abigail Hargreeves
characters.line: Reginald's alien wife, resurrected by the reset button; the reason he engineered the whole thing.

beats.label: S4 · Six years, no powers
beats.text: Six years after the reset the siblings live powerless, ordinary lives; Ben is just out of prison for a crypto scam and the family is barely in touch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the depowered, dispersed baseline — every reunion and every returning power in this season is measured against it.

beats.label: S4 · Keepers and a missing girl
beats.text: Five, now CIA, is investigating the Keepers — people who remember the erased timelines — when Sy Grossman asks Viktor to find his missing daughter Jennifer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Keepers and Jennifer are the two threads the season's plot rides on; the reader needs both entered together.

beats.label: S4 · Ben spikes the sake
beats.text: Ben secretly laces the family's sake with marigold, restoring everyone's powers overnight — except Klaus, who abstained and stays powerless.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The powers return by Ben's hand, not choice, which will matter as Ben's role in the finale unfolds.

beats.label: S4 · Jennifer, and the Cleanse
beats.text: They rescue Jennifer; Reginald and Abigail reveal Ben carries marigold and Jennifer carries durango, and when the two elements meet they trigger the reality-ending 'Cleanse'.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the season's central threat named and explained — it's the apocalypse the finale is built around.

beats.label: S4 · Fusion, and Abigail's confession
beats.text: Ben and Jennifer sleep together and begin fusing into the Cleanse; Abigail admits she engineered this because her resurrection was never meant to happen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The 'why' behind Reginald's whole reset scheme falls apart in one sentence — the antagonist becomes complicit in her own erasure.

beats.label: S4 · The marigold made everything
beats.text: Five learns from parallel versions of himself that Reginald's 1989 marigold experiment created every timeline and caused every apocalypse the family ever lived through.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the entire series in a single beat and hands the siblings the case for stepping into the Cleanse themselves.

beats.label: S4 · One timeline
beats.text: Lila saves her family and Claire; the siblings surrender to the Cleanse, dissolving the multiverse to leave a single timeline — where marigold blooms beneath a giant sycamore.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The finale. The cost of ending the cycle is the siblings themselves, and the closing image asks whether the cycle is really over.

cliffhanger.text: The siblings have stepped into the Cleanse and let it consume them and Ben, collapsing every timeline into one. A cluster of real marigold flowers has blossomed beneath a giant sycamore in the surviving world, generating pollen that looks a lot like the elixir that started everything.
questions: Are the Umbrella siblings truly gone, or does their sacrifice preserve them somewhere?
What does the marigold blooming beneath the sycamore mean for this one remaining world?
Could the cycle of marigold-born children begin again in this timeline?

characters.name: Number Five
characters.line: CIA agent chasing the Keepers; the sibling who works out the marigold is the source of every timeline and every apocalypse.

characters.name: Luther
characters.line: Powerless and working as a stripper at season start; got his powers back briefly before the family agreed to end them for good.

characters.name: Diego
characters.line: Out-of-shape delivery driver married to Lila with kids; wanted to be CIA and instead becomes one of the siblings who steps into the Cleanse.

characters.name: Allison
characters.line: Was doing commercials and raising Claire in peace after the reset; walks into the Cleanse alongside her siblings.

characters.name: Klaus
characters.line: Sober germaphobe who initially skipped the marigold saké but was dosed by Ben to save his life; later tortured by his old dealer Quinn after Quinn discovered his immortality.

characters.name: Viktor
characters.line: Runs a bar far from everyone; the sibling Sy Grossman approached about finding Jennifer, and the one who most tried to save Ben.

characters.name: Lila
characters.line: Diego's wife and mother of his children; saved her family and Claire before joining the siblings in the Cleanse.

characters.name: Ben
characters.line: Fused with Jennifer into the Cleanse; the marigold-durango pair that would have erased everything until the siblings absorbed it with them.

characters.name: Reginald and Abigail Hargreeves
characters.line: The reset couple who built this timeline for themselves; Abigail turned out to be the one steering things toward the Cleanse to undo her own resurrection.

characters.name: Jean and Gene Thibedeau
characters.line: The Keepers Five was investigating — cultists who remembered the erased timelines and had built their group around Jennifer.
